experimentPointer.name: EX01190 - BATCH01-with-dups
experimentPointer.description: This experiment contains samples from human subjects, both adults and children, participating in the Molecular Transducers of Physical Activity Consortium (MoTrPAC), an NIH-funded, multi-institution consortium which aims to develop a “map” of the molecular responses to exercise. This sample batch was collected during the "Pre-COVID" period (2019-Mar 2020). It consists of human plasma samples, 50 uL each, except for those slated for both untargeted metabolomics and steroid analysis, which contain 250uL each. Most samples were collected from sedentary adults and children. Some samples are from "highly active" adults and children, who were considered to be in an exercise-trained state according to study-defined parameters. Sedentary adults were randomized to participate either in an aerobic (running/cycling) or resistance (weight training) 12-week exercise training program, or to serve as controls. Sedentary children were only randomized between aerobic exercise training and controls. Neither highly active nor control subjects initiated exercise training. Due to COVID-related lab shutdowns in Mar 2020, the majority of the subjects randomized to a training intervention completed only the pre-training sample collection and were unable to complete training and post-training sample collection. Thus, only a few subjects have both pre- and post-training samples in this sample tranche. All sample collection was performed before, during and after a single bout of stationary cycling exercise. Subjects had multiple samples collected with each exercise bout, including pre-exercise, mid-exercise, "immediate" post-exercise and several post-exercise timepoints, yielding an average of ~7 samples per subject per exercise bout. Blood samples were collected as per MoTrPAC protocol into an EDTA-plasma collection tube and were centrifuged to generate plasma, which was aliquoted and frozen. Samples will be extracted according to MoTrPAC clinical sample extraction SOP and will be analyzed by RPLC untargeted (positive and negative ion modes) and ion pairing untargeted (negative ion mode). Samples will be analyzed "blinded" to all factors except to ensure all samples from a subject are in an analytical batch; randomization will be performed by our site batching officer in concert with a randomization algorithm developed by MoTrPAC BIC. For more details on the MoTrPAC study and protocols, see http://www.motrpac.org
